question: Which cell type contributes most strongly to the spatial transcriptome variance across arterial segments after integration with scRNA-seq data? If cell type annotations are needed, refer to 'author_cell_type'.

nodes.label: Confirm integrated representation linking Slide-seqV2 spots to scRNA-seq-derived author_cell_type annotations
Compute cell-type composition or dominant cell-type assignment per spatial spot from integrated data
Quantify spatial transcriptomic variance across arterial segments at the spot level
Model contribution of each cell type to spot-level transcriptomic variance across arterial segments
Identify the cell type with the largest explained variance and interpret its spatial pattern along arterial segments
Load integrated scRNA-seq–Slide-seqV2 AnnData object and verify that each Slide-seqV2 spot has mapped nearest-neighbor scRNA-seq cells with author_cell_type annotations
For each Slide-seqV2 spot, compute cell-type composition by aggregating author_cell_type of its mapped scRNA-seq neighbors and assign the dominant author_cell_type per spot

Quantify spot-level transcriptomic variance across arterial segments by computing per-gene variance of normalized expression within each segment and summarizing to a segment-wise variance score per spot

Fit a linear mixed-effects or variance-partitioning model with spot-level expression (or leading PCs) as response and spot-wise cell-type composition/dominant author_cell_type plus arterial segment identity as predictors to estimate variance explained by each cell type across segments

Extract the cell type with the highest proportion of explained variance from the model, generate its spatial abundance/dominance map across Slide-seqV2 spots, and summarize its spatial trend along arterial segments
